The term "hydrophilic" is used to describe a compound that dissolves well in water. A hydrophilic compound can dissolve via a charged or uncharged subsection. Typical hydrophiles include ions, sugars, and proteins.
The term "lipophilic" is used to describe compounds that dissolve well in oils or fats. Typically, such compounds have a hydrocarbon section.

senses.definition: The term "amphipathic" is used to describe molecules that have at least one section that dissolves well in water and at least one that dissolves well in oil or fats. Phospholipids, which include certain molecules that are essential to cell walls, are one category of amphipath. Soaps and detergents are amphipathic compounds, which is how they emulsify oil and grease in water.

An emulsion is a mixture of two liquids that normally are immiscible but are dispersed into each other. The emulsion often is stabilized by a chemical agent (an "emulsifier" or " 乳[にゅう]化[か]剤[ざい][3]").

An ellipsoid is a set of points from the set defined by the equation: (x / a)2 + ( y / b)2 + (z / c)2 ≤ 1 The constants a, b, and c are the lengths of the semiaxes. This forms an ellipsoid centered at (0, 0, 0). If a = b = c, the shape is a sphere. If any two semiaxes are the same length, the shape is a spheroid.
